Verify the handoff is complete (task, intent, allowed scope, exclusions, required evidence, test mode, stop conditions); if incomplete, block and return. Attest c1.

postconditions.statement: crew context + glossary + handoff loaded; handoff complete

m1-records.title: records.py: four frozen dataclasses + SESSION_ORDER + session_ordinal
m1-records.imperative: Write tests/unit/physics/feature_view/test_records.py FIRST (session_ordinal orders FP1<FP2<FP3<Q and raises ValueError naming the unknown session_type + known set for a bad input; each of the four dataclasses is frozen and constructible with its documented fields including the RESERVED fields defaulting to None with their *_status='unresolved' sibling). Observe it fail (module doesn't exist yet) -- attest c1. Then create src/physics/feature_view/__init__.py and src/physics/feature_view/records.py per the handoff shape (WeekendStateRecord, CarBasisPosteriorRecord, LapEvidenceRecord, FeatureViewRow, SESSION_ORDER, session_ordinal) until the test is green -- command-check c2.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: test_records.py written and observed failing (module/symbols absent) -- manual attest

constraints: no src.evo_predictor import anywhere in src/physics/feature_view/
reserved fields (process_noise_link, parc_ferme_step, unit_class_residuals) always None in this gate, never computed

m2-store-skeleton.title: store.py: FeatureViewStore schema + insert_*/load_* mechanics
m2-store-skeleton.imperative: Write tests/unit/physics/feature_view/test_store.py FIRST (tmp_path db: must_exist=True raises FileNotFoundError before any connect/schema work when the file doesn't exist; a fresh store constructs a schema for all four tables; insert_* + load_* round-trip one row per table; reuse of effective_axis_sigma/UNRESOLVED_AXIS_SIGMA_FRAC/normalize_axis_status from estimate_store_fields is exercised, not reimplemented). Observe it fail -- attest c1. Then implement src/physics/feature_view/store.py: FeatureViewStore(db_path, *, must_exist=False) mirroring EstimateStore's shape, default db_path='data/feature_view.db' documented as the standalone NEW sqlite file (never physics_estimates.db), _connect/_init_schema/_migrate_missing_columns additive self-heal, plain INSERT only (module docstring states the divergence from EstimateStore's INSERT OR REPLACE explicitly), UNIQUE constraints per natural key (+model_version, +as_of_session for feature_view_rows), and load_* methods returning pandas DataFrames -- until test_store.py is green (c2).

preconditions.statement: records.py exists and its own tests pass

postconditions.statement: TDD red: test_store.py written and observed failing -- manual attest

constraints: plain INSERT only, never INSERT OR REPLACE
tests use tmp_path only, never a committed DB path

m3-append-only-gate.title: test_append_only_contract.py: append-only contract-freeze (THE protected gate test)
m3-append-only-gate.imperative: Write tests/unit/physics/feature_view/test_append_only_contract.py FIRST per the handoff's Close Criteria: write a FeatureViewRow at model_version=1 for one natural key, write a DIFFERENT row at model_version=2 for the SAME natural key, re-read the model_version=1 row and assert byte-identical to what was originally written (every field), AND assert a second write with identical natural key+model_version raises sqlite3.IntegrityError. Observe it fail against the current store (attest c1) -- if store.py already satisfies it because m2 over-built, that is fine, but the UNIQUE constraint enforcement must be verified for real (not a docstring claim), so if it is already green, still capture the real IntegrityError traceback as evidence. Add/adjust the UNIQUE constraint in store.py until real, then green (c2) with the exact IntegrityError traceback captured verbatim.

preconditions.statement: store.py insert/load mechanics pass their own tests

postconditions.statement: TDD red or immediate-pass-with-captured-real-exception: test_append_only_contract.py written and its IntegrityError path exercised against real sqlite3 -- manual attest, real traceback captured

constraints: a duplicate natural-key+model_version write MUST raise a real sqlite3.IntegrityError via a UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY constraint, never an application-level check substituting for it

m4-as-of-leakage-gate.title: test_as_of_leakage.py: as-of leakage prevention by construction + negative control (THE other protected gate test)
m4-as-of-leakage-gate.imperative: Write tests/unit/physics/feature_view/test_as_of_leakage.py FIRST per the handoff's Close Criteria: seed weekend_state_records/car_basis_posteriors for FP1/FP2/FP3/Q with distinct sentinel axis values across TWO different (year, gp_name, constructor) tuples; query 'as of FP1' via the store's as-of-scoped read method and assert only the FP1 sentinel returns per entity; capture every SQL statement via sqlite3.Connection.set_trace_callback (or equivalent) during that query and assert EVERY statement touching weekend_state_records/car_basis_posteriors has an explicit session restriction in its WHERE-clause TEXT (session_type IN (...) or session_ordinal <=); then write a deliberately-broken negative-control query in the TEST ITSELF (no session filter, Python-side post-filter) and assert the WHERE-clause-structure check correctly FAILS it. Observe the real test go red first (attest c1) -- if the negative control cannot be made to fail as designed, this is a STOP CONDITION: do not weaken the test, escalate instead. Implement the store's as-of-scoped query method (session bound as a REQUIRED, non-optional parameter) until real green (c2), capturing the full SQL statement list as evidence.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: test_as_of_leakage.py written, negative control proven to actually fail the assertion it claims to catch -- manual attest, captured SQL list evidence

constraints: as-of query method's session bound must be a required parameter, never optional/defaulted to all
the negative control must be a real broken query path proven to fail the check, not a tautology
